newsitem.title: USA: NY Fed McDonough says U.S. inflation not dead.
newsitem.headline: NY Fed McDonough says U.S. inflation not dead.

text.p: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President William McDonough said on Monday "only a fool" would believe U.S. inflation is dead.
"We must continue to be watchful because only a fool will think that (U.S.) inflation is dead," McDonough told a meeting of Matif, the French international futures and options exchange.
The next two years will present a challenging period for U.S. monetary policy makers, McDonough added.
"We must be very careful about looking 18 to 24 months into the future as to what the economy will do," he said.
McDonough asserted the sole goal of monetary policy "is to achieve sustainable economic growth," stressing the only way to reach that goal "is to achieve price stability."

McDonough hailed the recent rebound in U.S. manufacturing from what he called a "near-death" state, but noted the U.S. economy still faced "a structrual problem ... the inadequacy of the U.S. savings rate." --Isabelle Clary, 212-859-1666.
